title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E506 explains Lagrange's 1766–69 method for integrating the separated equation dx/√X = ±dy/√Y. In this 'Analysis' section Euler applies the method to the even sextic X = B + Cx² + Dx⁴ + Ex⁶, with Y the same polynomial in y.

Setup (previous page). Put dx/√X = dt, so dx²/dt² = X and dy²/dt² = Y. Introduce p = (x²+y²)/2 and q = (x²−y²)/2, so dp = x dx + y dy and dq = x dx − y dy. Then dp·dq/(2q dt²) = (x²X − y²Y)/(x²−y²) = B + 2Cp + D(3p²+q²) + 4E(p³+pq²). Differentiating with dt constant gives 2ddx/dt² = X' and 2ddy/dt² = Y'.

This page.
- Combining with the squared first derivatives: 2 d(x dx)/dt² = xX' + 2X, and likewise for y.
- Adding the two: 2 ddp/dt² = xX' + yY' + 2(X+Y).
- Using x² = p+q and y² = p−q, so that x⁴+y⁴ = 2(p²+q²) and x⁶+y⁶ = 2p(p²+3q²):
  - 2X + 2Y = 4B + 4Cp + 4D(p²+q²) + 4Ep(p²+3q²);
  - xX' + yY' = 4Cp + 8D(p²+q²) + 12Ep(p²+3q²).
- Hence 2 ddp/dt² = 4B + 8Cp + 12D(p²+q²) + 16Ep(p²+3q²).

§75. Subtract four times the first-order relation. The B and C terms cancel exactly, leaving
2 ddp/dt² − 2 dp dq/(q dt²) = 8Dq² + 32Epq².
Multiplying by dp/q² turns the left side into the exact differential d(dp²/(q² dt²)). Integrating gives
dp²/(q² dt²) = 4Δ + 8Dp + 16Ep²,
and taking the root, dp/(q dt) = 2√(Δ + 2Dp + 4Ep²).

§76. Substitute back dp/dt = x√X ∓ y√Y and 2q = x² − y². This yields the algebraic first integral (complete integral of the addition-theorem type):
(x√X ∓ y√Y)/(x²−y²) = √(Δ + D(x²+y²) + E(x²+y²)²).
The next page squares this, simplifies, and fixes Δ by the condition that y = 0 gives x = k.

Purpose: to show that Lagrange's 'mechanical' trick (treat the separated equation as two equations of motion in a common time t, then find a second integral) yields Euler's own algebraic integral for dx/√X = dy/√Y beyond the quartic case. This even-sextic case is really the elliptic (quartic) case after u = x², and the result is checked against the integral of §72.
errors: In the printed line for xX' + yY' the last term carries a minus sign ('− 12Ep(pp+3qq)'). It should be +12Ep(pp+3qq), as Euler himself uses in the combined result (+16E…). This is a typographical error in the original.
On the previous page the section is printed as '§. 64'; it should be §. 74. This is a misprint.
No mathematical errors otherwise: every algebraic identity on the page checks out, including the cancellations of B and C in §75.

ideas.what: Treating the separated differential equation as a pair of 'motions' in a common parameter t and passing to second-order equations to find a further integral (Lagrange's method)
ideas.modern_name: Lagrange's dynamical derivation of the Euler addition theorem for elliptic integrals (integrable two-particle system / first-integral method)
ideas.usually_credited_to: J.-L. Lagrange (Misc. Taurinensia IV, 1766–69); explained by Euler in E506
ideas.where_published: E506 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Petrop. 1778 [1781]), Opera omnia I.21; Lagrange's original memoir

ideas.what: Change of variables p = (x²+y²)/2, q = (x²−y²)/2 adapted to the even sextic, with an integrating factor dp/q² making the combination an exact differential
ideas.modern_name: Symmetric-function coordinates; integrating factor for the reduced ODE
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (with u = x+y, v = x−y style variables); adapted by Euler

ideas.modern_name: Addition theorem for elliptic integrals (the even sextic reduces to genus 1 via u = x²)
ideas.where_published: E506 §72 and here; related forms in Euler's Institutiones calculi integralis I (E342) and E251/E252-era papers on elliptic integrals

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine verification within a well-known paper (E506, Opera omnia I.21) of a known integral. The sextic case is the quartic/elliptic case in disguise, and nothing here goes beyond the recorded history of the Euler–Lagrange addition theorem.
transcription_corrections: The line 'xX' + yY' = 4Cp + 8D(pp+qq) + 12Ep(pp+3qq)' reads in the image as '… − 12Ep(pp+3qq)'. The printed minus is a typo in the original, and the transcription silently corrected it.
The previous-page section number '§. 64' should be §. 74, matching the sequence §73, §75, §76.
